My land is about 6 mu here on the flat plain. I have farmed this ground for over forty years, first with my husband, now alone. My children left for the city long ago. I am slower now at 68, but I know this soil. My knees hurt in cold weather, so I rely on the village machinery cooperative for plowing and harvesting — I pay them to do it, I cannot manage that equipment myself anymore.

I will grow winter wheat and summer corn, same as every year, same as my neighbors. Same land, both seasons. That is what this ground is for. I will also keep a small vegetable patch near the house for my own food — garlic, scallions, a few rows of Chinese cabbage. I do not count that in my plans, it is just the kitchen garden.

For wheat, I will buy seed from the village agro-shop, whatever improved variety Brother Liu has in stock — he knows what grows well here. I will spread compound fertilizer before planting and add urea in spring when the wheat greens up. I will irrigate three times: once before winter sets hard, once at jointing, once when the heads are filling. I will spray once for weeds in early spring and once for aphids and rust before harvest. I use rotary tillage before sowing — the cooperative does it.

For corn, I plant right after wheat comes off in June. No time to waste. I will use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has. I scatter fertilizer at planting and top-dress once when the corn is knee-high. I only irrigate if the sky is dry — usually once at planting if the ground is parched. I spray herbicide and watch for the armyworm. No deep tillage for corn, I just let the stalks get rolled and direct-seed.

I do not experiment. I do not try new things. At my age, a bad harvest is something I cannot recover from.
